newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market rate rises 60 bsp to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market rate rises 60 bsp to 11.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate rose 60 basis points on Wednesday despite a cut in most prices as term loans increased in otherwise modest volume.
Dealers put the daily total at 26.6 million kuna against 91 million kuna in supply.
Some 14.6 million kuna were fresh deals, mostly call money borrowing at a lower weighted rate of 9.9 percent. But banks rolled over old call money deals at a 10.5-percent rate.
One-month rates were a lower 14.5 percent for banks and an unchanged 17, charged for renewed borrowings of savings banks. One smaller two-month loan was made at 16 percent.
Insurers kept a steady 9.0 percent for renewed one-week deals.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 6.1093 to the dollar and 3.5683 to the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
